# Role
You are a Code Agent, an autonomous software engineer. From a structured architecture specification
(spec.json, preprocessed from an architecture document and UML views) you design, implement, test and
document the complete Python desktop application it describes, in the project directory you are given.
You work only through the provided tools.

# Rules
1. Target is a single-user Windows DESKTOP application built with Tkinter. Never build a web app,
   server, REST/gRPC service, Docker-only or cloud deployment. If the input describes a web /
   microservice / cloud system, keep its LOGICAL design (components, use cases, classes, states,
   sequences, data entities) and ADAPT the technology to a desktop app. Record every adaptation.
2. Python standard library only, and ONLY these modules (they are bundled in the user's exe; anything
   else will not exist on the target PC): tkinter, tkinter.ttk, tkinter.messagebox, tkinter.simpledialog, tkinter.filedialog, tkinter.font, tkinter.colorchooser, sqlite3, json, csv, fractions, decimal, random, math, statistics, dataclasses, enum, abc, typing, collections, itertools, functools, operator, datetime, time, pathlib, os, sys, re, string, textwrap, uuid, copy, logging, tempfile, shutil, contextlib, threading, queue, unittest, unittest.mock, io, traceback, heapq, bisect, pprint, argparse, configparser, hashlib, importlib.
   Tests use pytest. No third-party runtime packages, no network access.
3. Keep domain logic free of Tkinter (pure Python, testable headless); the UI layer calls the logic.
4. Prefer edit_file (exact, unique search-and-replace) over rewriting a file. You must read_file a
   whole file before editing it. Create new files with write_files, several per call.
5. Be request-efficient: every model call costs money. Batch independent tool calls in one turn,
   write many files per write_files call, plan once, fix all reported errors in one round.
6. Paths are relative to the project root. The folder agent_run/ belongs to the harness (read-only).
7. Never run main.py or anything that opens a window or waits for input; tests must not need a display.
8. Keep AGENT_NOTES.md (your memory file) up to date with key decisions when they change.
9. Build what the spec describes. Where it is thin, derive reasonable behaviour from the use cases,
   diagrams and prose (e.g. features named only in a summary) and document each assumption.
   A task profile, if provided, adds hints; the spec still wins on anything it states explicitly.

# UI quality rules (any desktop app)
- Main window: at least 1100x750 (root.minsize(1100, 750)), resizable, centred, and opened MAXIMIZED on
  Windows: try root.state("zoomed") except tk.TclError: root.attributes("-zoomed", True). F11 toggles
  full screen (root.attributes("-fullscreen", …)) and Esc leaves full screen. Never a tiny dialog-sized window.
- Large readable fonts: titles 32+ pt, main content / questions 24-28+ pt, buttons and inputs 18+ pt.
- One consistent colour theme that suits the domain, high-contrast text. Big buttons with generous padding,
  flat relief and a hover colour (bind <Enter>/<Leave> or set activebackground).
- Forms: the main input has keyboard focus, Enter submits, the input is cleared automatically after each
  submission, and feedback is clear and coloured (green = success, red = error) in the window itself.
  Use messagebox only for confirmations.
- Each screen is its own Frame class in ui/, switched by one app/controller object. Expose a factory such as
  `create_app(root) -> App` that builds everything WITHOUT calling mainloop(), so tests can build the UI.
- Required test tests/test_ui_smoke.py (pytest): create ONE tk.Tk() for the whole session (session-scoped
  fixture; retry 3 times, then pytest.skip on tk.TclError). Never destroy and re-create Tk between tests —
  that can crash on Windows; instead cancel pending root.after() callbacks and destroy the root's children
  after each test, and destroy the root once at the end. root.withdraw(),
  build the app with the factory, call root.update_idletasks(), assert root.minsize() >= (1100, 750), show every
  screen in turn and assert its key widgets exist (title label, main buttons, inputs), exercise one form
  submission (input cleared, feedback shown), then root.destroy(). This catches poor or broken UIs.

# Tool usage
- update_todos: keep a todo list; exactly one item in_progress; mark items completed as you go.
- PLAN phase: only read-only tools, update_todos and submit_plan are allowed.
- IMPLEMENT / FIX phase: write_files, edit_file, run_python(compile|test), update_todos, then finish.
- Before finish: run_python action=compile and action=test yourself and fix failures.
- Tool errors come back as results starting with 'Error:'; read them and correct the call.

# Output contract (applies to any input spec)
Implement every use case, class, state machine, sequence and component in spec.domain_model, plus
features that appear only in prose (domain_model.implied_features). Launch with `python main.py`.

Project layout:
  main.py               entry point; the only module that starts Tk
  <package>/            one Python package per logical component / UML package (snake_case names),
                        keeping the class, attribute and method names of the class diagram; services
                        that were REST/gRPC become in-process Python interfaces with the same operations
  ui/                   Tkinter screens / dialogs, one per use case or major state
  sql/schema.sql        if the spec has persisted entities or DDL: SQLite DDL adapted from it
  data/                 seed data files, if the application needs initial content
  tests/                pytest, headless: domain logic, every state machine (valid AND invalid
                        transitions), sequences, persistence with a temporary SQLite file, plus the
                        required UI smoke test tests/test_ui_smoke.py (see UI quality rules)
  README.md             what it is, how to run and test, features, UML → module mapping
  DESIGN_DECISIONS.md   written by the harness from your submit_plan (see below)
  TRACEABILITY.csv      columns: requirement,use_case_or_feature,component,file,test — one row per
                        requirement id, use case and implied feature
  requirements.txt      "# standard library only" plus pytest
  Dockerfile            optional: python:3.12-slim running the tests headless
  AGENT_NOTES.md        your memory file

DESIGN_DECISIONS.md must contain:
  1. Adaptation table: original element → desktop equivalent → reason, covering every term in
     spec.platform_conflicts and every API contract / data store / infrastructure item in the spec.
  2. "Input issues found": every item in spec.input_issues, each with how you handled it.
  3. Assumptions made where the spec is thin.
  4. UML → code mapping (diagram element → module / class / test).

# Task profile: Space Fractions (selected by the user)
Additional task-specific hints:

Optional hints for the Space Fractions architecture documents (an educational fractions game for
6th-grade students). These complement spec.json; they do not replace it.

Screens / flow
- Animated INTRO scene (the "introductory movie"): space-themed tkinter.Canvas animation (stars, ship),
  a Skip button, auto-advances to the menu.
- MAIN MENU: Play, High Scores, Help, Admin, Exit.
- PLAYER NAME entry before playing (UserComponent).
- QUESTION FLOW: a round of fraction questions of mixed types — equivalent fractions, compare,
  add/subtract, simplify; multiple choice and typed answers; immediate feedback; progress and score.
  Check correctness with fractions.Fraction so equivalent forms are accepted (2/4 == 1/2).
- PAUSE / RESUME following the state diagram Playing ⇄ Paused → GameOver (invalid transitions raise).
- ENDING scene with final score, percentage and encouraging feedback; option to play again.
- HIGH SCORES (View Score) from SQLite; HELP screen (View Help); ADMIN screen to add / edit / delete
  questions (Update Questions).

Kid-friendly look and feel (players are 11–12 years old; this matters as much as correctness)
- Opens maximized (minimum 1100x750), F11 full screen, Esc leaves full screen.
- Space theme on a tkinter.Canvas background: dark blue (#0B1736-ish), twinkling stars, two or three
  colourful planets drawn with ovals/arcs. Bright accent colours (yellow, cyan, pink, green) on dark panels.
- Fonts: titles 36+ pt bold, questions 30 pt, answer input and buttons 20+ pt. Big flat buttons with a
  hover colour; multiple-choice answers as 2x2 big coloured buttons.
- Question screen: "Question 3 of 10" progress text plus a progress bar, the score always visible, the answer
  input focused, Enter submits, and a visible Pause button (state machine Paused shows an overlay with Resume).
- After every answer: big coloured feedback in the window — green "Correct! 🎉" or red
  "Not quite — the answer is 3/4" — the input is CLEARED automatically and the next question appears after
  about a second (no manual clearing, no popup).
- End screen: big "Congratulations, <name>!", the score and percentage, 1–3 stars earned (by percentage),
  a short Canvas confetti/star animation, and buttons "Play again" / "Main menu".
- Intro: animated rocket flying across moving stars with the game title, a Skip button, auto-advance.
- tests/test_ui_smoke.py must build every screen (intro, menu, name entry, question, pause overlay, end,
  high scores, help, admin) and check the answer input is cleared after a submission.

Data
- `data/questions.json`: at least 20 seed questions covering all four question types.
- `sql/schema.sql`: adapt the document's `games` table and add `questions` and `scores` tables.

Packages
- `game/` (Game, state machine, scoring), `questions/` (Question, answer checking, repository),
  `users/`, `admin/`, `ui/` — mirroring GameComponent, QuestionComponent, UserComponent, AdminComponent.

Required files for this task: sql/schema.sql, data/questions.json

## PHASE 1/3 — ANALYSE & PLAN (plan mode: read-only)

1. Call update_todos with the implementation plan (8–15 concrete items, first one in_progress).

   - notes: short content for AGENT_NOTES.md (key decisions, module responsibilities, conventions).
You may call both tools in the same turn.

## 1. Adaptation table (original element → desktop equivalent → reason)

| Original element | Desktop equivalent | Reason |
|---|---|---|
| web-based / microservices (Node.js, Express.js) | Single Tkinter desktop app, in-process Python packages | Task constraint: single-user Windows desktop application. Components become Python packages (`game/`, `questions/`, `users/`, `admin/`, `ui/`). |
| RESTful API (`openapi.yaml` `/play`) | In-process `GameComponent` with `play()` / `view_score()` operations | No network needed; UI calls logic directly. Same logical operations preserved. |
| gRPC `GameService.Play` (`internal.proto`) | `Game.play()` method (sync, in-process) | RPC becomes a plain method call; latency is negligible in-process so NFR-1 (performance) is trivially met and testable. |
| PostgreSQL `games` table (JSONB state) | SQLite `games` table with a TEXT `game_state` (JSON) column | Single-user persistence; SQLite file bundled with app. Adapted in `sql/schema.sql`. |
| Redis (cache) | In-memory caches (dict) in repositories | No distributed cache needed; seed questions loaded once into memory. |
| RabbitMQ (messaging) | Direct method calls / callback in UI controller | No asynchronous service boundaries. |
| Elasticsearch (search) | In-memory Python list scan | Question set is small (seed + admin-added). |
| OAuth2 (authn/authz) | Local username entry + admin PIN; user role field | Single local user per session; Admin screen gated by a PIN (default `space-admin`). |
| Prometheus (observability) | `logging` module + score persistence | Local monitoring suffices. |
| Jenkins / Docker / Terraform / Kubernetes / Istio / Vault / TLS / replicas | Removed; plain Python stdlib app | No CI/CD, container orchestration or infra needed for a desktop app. |
| Node.js runtime | Python 3.11+ (stdlib only) | Bundled in the user's exe; target platform mandates stdlib-only. |
| ASR-1 data durability (PostgreSQL backups/replication) | SQLite file + periodic `commit()` + seed JSON backup | Data durability via local file; `data/questions.json` seed and admin edits persisted to DB. |
| ASR-2 security | Admin PIN, local input, no network exposure | No remote attack surface in a single-user desktop app. |

## 2. Input issues found

- **EMPTY_TABLE** (high): The testing matrix has headers but empty cells. → I mapped each test type to relevant components myself: Unit (Game, Question, User, Admin), Integration (repository↔logic↔DB), Contract (component interfaces/state machine), E2E (UI smoke), Chaos (invalid state transitions + corrupt DB recovery). Documented in TRACEABILITY.csv/test files.
- **ARTIFACT_MISMATCH** (medium): ASR-1 references `sql/question_ddl.sql` but deliverables list `sql/game_ddl.sql`. → Adapting the document's `games` table and additionally creating `questions` and `scores` tables in a single `sql/schema.sql`, satisfying both the `games` DDL and question persistence (ASR-1).
- **THIN_REQUIREMENTS** (high): Only 4 requirement IDs; implied features (intro, menu, questions, ending) have no FRs. → Derived FRs (FR-2…FR-8) for each implied feature and recorded in TRACEABILITY.csv with their components/tests.
- **UNTRACED_REQUIREMENT** (medium): ASR-2 not in traceability matrix. → Added ASR-2 row (Admin PIN / local auth) mapping to `users/` + `admin/` + tests.
- **GENERIC_JUSTIFICATIONS** (medium): 12 copy-pasted justifications. → Noted; each tech item mapped in the adaptation table above with a specific reason.
- **DUPLICATE_BLOCKS** (low): 4 duplicated code blocks. → Deduplicated: single schema, single API/proto description consolidated; no functional impact.
- **PLATFORM_CONFLICT** (high): web/cloud → desktop. → Fully re-targeted per adaptation table (this is the core constraint).

def big_button(parent, text, command=None, bg=CYAN, fg=BG, size=20, width=None, pady=14):
    """Large flat button with hover colour."""
    btn = tk.Button(
        parent,
        text=text,
        command=command,
        bg=bg,
        fg=fg,
        font=font(size, "bold"),
        relief="flat",
        activebackground=bg,

        btn.configure(width=width)

    darker = _blend(bg, "#000000", 0.15)
    btn.bind("<Enter>", lambda e: btn.configure(bg=darker))
    btn.bind("<Leave>", lambda e: btn.configure(bg=bg))
    return btn


def _blend(hex_a, hex_b, t):
    """Blend two #RRGGBB colours, t = amount of b (0..1)."""
    a = hex_a.lstrip("#")
    b = hex_b.lstrip("#")
    ra, ga_, ba = int(a[0:2], 16), int(a[2:4], 16), int(a[4:6], 16)
    rb, gb, bb = int(b[0:2], 16), int(b[2:4], 16), int(b[4:6], 16)
    r = int(ra + (rb - ra) * t)
    g = int(ga_ + (gb - ga_) * t)
    bl = int(ba + (bb - ba) * t)
    return f"#{r:02X}{g:02X}{bl:02X}"

class App:
    """Owns the root window, repositories, and screen switching."""

    DB_PATH = "data/spacefractions.db"

    def __init__(self, root: tk.Tk, db_path: str | None = None):
        self.root = root
        self.db_path = db_path or App.DB_PATH
        self.questions = QuestionRepository(self.db_path)
        self.scores = ScoreRepository(self.db_path)

        self.username: str = ""
        self.user: User | None = None
        self.game: Game | None = None
        self.round_questions: list = []
        self.current_index: int = 0

        self._screens = {}
        self._current = None

        self.root.bind("<F11>", self._toggle_fullscreen)
        self.root.bind("<Escape>", self._leave_fullscreen)

    # ---- navigation ----
    def register(self, name: str, screen) -> None:
        self._screens[name] = screen

    def show(self, name: str) -> None:
        if self._current is not None:
            self._current.pack_forget()
        screen = self._screens[name]
        screen.refresh()
        screen.pack(fill="both", expand=True)
        self._current = screen

    # ---- fullscreen ----
    def _toggle_fullscreen(self, _event=None) -> None:
        state = self.root.attributes("-fullscreen")
        self.root.attributes("-fullscreen", not state)

    def _leave_fullscreen(self, _event=None) -> None:
        self.root.attributes("-fullscreen", False)

    # ---- game flow helpers ----
    def start_round(self, count: int = 10) -> None:
        self.game = Game(game_id="round")
        self.round_questions = self.questions.sample(count)
        self.current_index = 0

    def next_question(self):
        if self.game is None or self.current_index >= len(self.round_questions):
            return None
        q = self.round_questions[self.current_index]
        self.current_index += 1
        return q

    def remaining(self) -> int:
        return max(0, len(self.round_questions) - self.current_index)

    def save_score(self) -> None:
        if not self.game or not self.username:
            return
        self.scores.add_score(
            self.username,
            self.game.score,
            self.game.total,
            self.game.percentage(),
            self.game.stars(),

        )
        self.progress_text.grid(row=0, column=0, padx=20, pady=8, sticky="w")

        )
        self.pause_btn.grid(row=0, column=2, padx=20, pady=8, sticky="e")

        self.progress = tk.ttk.Progressbar(self.topbar, length=300, maximum=10)
        self.progress.grid(row=0, column=3, padx=20, pady=8)

        self.topbar.grid_columnconfigure(3, weight=1)

        # Question area
        self.question_label = tk.Label(
            self.canvas, text="", bg=theme.BG, fg=theme.TEXT,
            font=theme.font(30, "bold"), wraplength=900, justify="center",
        )

            self.canvas, text="", bg=theme.BG, fg=theme.GREEN,
            font=theme.font(26, "bold"),
        )
        self.canvas.create_window(550, 340, window=self.feedback)

        self.entry = tk.Entry(
            self.canvas, textvariable=self.answer_var, font=theme.font(22),
            width=20, justify="center",
        )
        self.canvas.create_window(550, 430, window=self.entry)
        self.entry.bind("<Return>", lambda e: self._submit())

        self.submit_btn = theme.big_button(
            self.canvas, "Submit", command=self._submit, bg=theme.CYAN,
        )
        self.canvas.create_window(550, 520, window=self.submit_btn)

        # Multiple-choice option buttons (2x2 grid)
        self.option_frame = tk.Frame(self.canvas, bg=theme.BG)
        self.canvas.create_window(550, 430, window=self.option_frame)
        self._option_btns = []

    def refresh(self) -> None:
        self.canvas.draw_background()
        self.canvas.twinkle()
        self._cancel_advance()
        self.app.start_round(10)
        self._show_next()

    def _show_next(self) -> None:
        q = self.app.next_question()
        if q is None:
            self._finish()
            return
        self._current_question = q
        idx = self.app.current_index
        total = len(self.app.round_questions)
        self.progress_text.configure(text=f"Question {idx} of {total}")
        self.progress.configure(maximum=total, value=idx - 1)
        self.score_text.configure(text=f"Score: {self.app.game.score}")
        self.feedback.configure(text="")
        self.answer_var.set("")
        self.question_label.configure(text=q.prompt)

        if q.is_multiple_choice():
            self._build_options(q)
            self.entry.place_forget()
            self.option_frame.place(x=550, y=430, anchor="center")
            self.canvas.delete("submit_placeholder")
        else:
            self._clear_options()
            self.option_frame.place_forget()
            self.entry.place(x=550, y=430, anchor="center")
            self.entry.focus_set()

    def _build_options(self, q) -> None:
        self._clear_options()
        self._option_btns = []
        colours = [theme.YELLOW, theme.CYAN, theme.PINK, theme.GREEN]
        for i, opt in enumerate(q.options):
            btn = theme.big_button(
                self.option_frame, opt, command=lambda o=opt: self._answer(o),
                bg=colours[i % len(colours)], width=16, size=18, pady=10,
            )
            btn.grid(row=i // 2, column=i % 2, padx=10, pady=10)
            self._option_btns.append(btn)

    def _clear_options(self) -> None:
        for b in self._option_btns:
            b.destroy()
        self._option_btns = []

    def _answer(self, value: str) -> None:
        self.answer_var.set(value)
        self._submit()

    def _submit(self) -> None:
        if self._current_question is None:
            return
        answer = self.answer_var.get().strip()
        if not answer:
            self.feedback.configure(text="Type an answer first!", fg=theme.RED)
            return
        correct = check_answer(self._current_question.answer, answer)
        self.app.game.record_answer(correct)
        self.score_text.configure(text=f"Score: {self.app.game.score}")
        if correct:
            self.feedback.configure(text="Correct! 🎉", fg=theme.GREEN)
        else:
            self.feedback.configure(
                text=f"Not quite — the answer is {self._current_question.answer}",
                fg=theme.RED,
            )
        self.answer_var.set("")  # cleared automatically
        self._pending_advance = self.after(1200, self._show_next)

    def _pause(self) -> None:
        try:
            self.app.game.pause()
        except Exception:
            return
        self.app.show("pause")

    def _finish(self) -> None:
        try:
            self.app.game.game_over()
        except Exception:
            pass
        self.app.save_score()
        self.app.show("end")

    def _cancel_advance(self) -> None:
        if self._pending_advance is not None:
            try:
                self.after_cancel(self._pending_advance)
            except tk.TclError:
                pass
            self._pending_advance = None

# DESIGN DECISIONS — Space Fractions

## 1. Adaptation table (original element → desktop equivalent → reason)

| Original element | Desktop equivalent | Reason |
|---|---|---|
| web-based / microservices (Node.js, Express.js) | Single Tkinter desktop app, in-process Python packages | Task constraint: single-user Windows desktop application. Components become Python packages (`game/`, `questions/`, `users/`, `admin/`, `ui/`). |
| RESTful API (`openapi.yaml` `/play`) | In-process `GameComponent` with `play()` / `view_score()` operations | No network needed; UI calls logic directly. Same logical operations preserved. |
| gRPC `GameService.Play` (`internal.proto`) | `Game.play()` method (sync, in-process) | RPC becomes a plain method call; latency is negligible in-process so NFR-1 (performance) is trivially met and testable. |
| PostgreSQL `games` table (JSONB state) | SQLite `games` table with a TEXT `game_state` (JSON) column | Single-user persistence; SQLite file bundled with app. Adapted in `sql/schema.sql`. |
| Redis (cache) | In-memory caches (dict) in repositories | No distributed cache needed; seed questions loaded once into memory. |
| RabbitMQ (messaging) | Direct method calls / callback in UI controller | No asynchronous service boundaries. |
| Elasticsearch (search) | In-memory Python list scan | Question set is small (seed + admin-added). |
| OAuth2 (authn/authz) | Local username entry + admin PIN; user role field | Single local user per session; Admin screen gated by a PIN (default `space-admin`). |
| Prometheus (observability) | `logging` module + score persistence | Local monitoring suffices. |
| Jenkins / Docker / Terraform / Kubernetes / Istio / Vault / TLS / replicas | Removed; plain Python stdlib app | No CI/CD, container orchestration or infra needed for a desktop app. |
| Node.js runtime | Python 3.11+ (stdlib only) | Bundled in the user's exe; target platform mandates stdlib-only. |
| ASR-1 data durability (PostgreSQL backups/replication) | SQLite file + periodic `commit()` + seed JSON backup | Data durability via local file; `data/questions.json` seed and admin edits persisted to DB. |
| ASR-2 security | Admin PIN, local input, no network exposure | No remote attack surface in a single-user desktop app. |

## 2. Input issues found

- **EMPTY_TABLE** (high): The testing matrix has headers but empty cells. → I mapped each test type to relevant components myself: Unit (Game, Question, User, Admin), Integration (repository↔logic↔DB), Contract (component interfaces/state machine), E2E (UI smoke), Chaos (invalid state transitions + corrupt DB recovery). Documented in TRACEABILITY.csv/test files.
- **ARTIFACT_MISMATCH** (medium): ASR-1 references `sql/question_ddl.sql` but deliverables list `sql/game_ddl.sql`. → Adapting the document's `games` table and additionally creating `questions` and `scores` tables in a single `sql/schema.sql`, satisfying both the `games` DDL and question persistence (ASR-1).
- **THIN_REQUIREMENTS** (high): Only 4 requirement IDs; implied features (intro, menu, questions, ending) have no FRs. → Derived FRs (FR-2…FR-8) for each implied feature and recorded in TRACEABILITY.csv with their components/tests.
- **UNTRACED_REQUIREMENT** (medium): ASR-2 not in traceability matrix. → Added ASR-2 row (Admin PIN / local auth) mapping to `users/` + `admin/` + tests.
- **GENERIC_JUSTIFICATIONS** (medium): 12 copy-pasted justifications. → Noted; each tech item mapped in the adaptation table above with a specific reason.
- **DUPLICATE_BLOCKS** (low): 4 duplicated code blocks. → Deduplicated: single schema, single API/proto description consolidated; no functional impact.
- **PLATFORM_CONFLICT** (high): web/cloud → desktop. → Fully re-targeted per adaptation table (this is the core constraint).
- **UML_SYNTAX** (low): Mermaid `->>` arrows and `artifact`/`participant` misuse. → Normalised to PlantUML-style `->`; diagram semantics (sequence: play flow + admin update) preserved in domain model and implemented.

## 3. Assumptions made where the spec is thin

- The game is a **round of 10 fraction questions**, selected randomly from the question pool covering all four types (equivalent fractions, compare, add/subtract, simplify).
- **Answer checking** uses `fractions.Fraction` so equivalent forms are accepted (e.g. `2/4` equals `1/2`), including typed answers and multiple choice.
- **Scoring**: 1 point per correct answer; final percentage = correct/answered; 1–3 stars earned by percentage (≥50% 1★, ≥75% 2★, ≥90% 3★).
- **State machine** enforces only valid transitions: `[*]→Playing`, `Playing⇄Paused`, `Playing→GameOver`; `pause()` from GameOver or Paused, `resume()` from Playing/GameOver, and `gameOver()` from Paused raise `InvalidTransitionError`.
- **Admin** is gated by a PIN (default `space-admin`); Admin can add/edit/delete questions (Update Questions use case).
- **User** authentication: player enters a name (optional high-score persistence); Admin is a built-in role.
- **Persistence**: SQLite DB (`data/spacefractions.db`) created from `sql/schema.sql`; seed questions loaded from `data/questions.json` on first run.
- **Intro** auto-advances to the menu after ~5s or via Skip button.

## 4. UML → code mapping

| Diagram element | Module / class | Test |
|---|---|---|
| Game class (+play, viewScore) | `game/game.py` → `Game` | `tests/test_game.py` |
| Question class (+getPrompt, getOptions) | `questions/question.py` → `Question` | `tests/test_questions.py` |
| User class (+playGame, viewScore) | `users/user.py` → `User` | `tests/test_users.py` |
| Admin class (+updateQuestions) | `admin/admin.py` → `Admin` | `tests/test_admin.py` |
| State machine (Playing/Paused/GameOver) | `game/state.py` → `GameState`, `InvalidTransitionError` | `tests/test_state.py` |
| SequenceDiagram1 (play flow) | `game/game.py` + `questions/` + `ui/question_screen.py` | integration + UI smoke |
| SequenceDiagram2 (admin update) | `admin/admin.py` + `questions/repository.py` | `tests/test_admin.py` |
| UseCase: Play Game | `ui/menu_screen.py`, `ui/question_screen.py`, `game/game.py` | `tests/test_ui_smoke.py` |
| UseCase: View Score | `ui/highscores_screen.py`, `users/repository.py` | `tests/test_scores.py` |
| UseCase: View Help | `ui/help_screen.py` | `tests/test_ui_smoke.py` |
| UseCase: Update Questions | `ui/admin_screen.py`, `admin/admin.py` | `tests/test_admin.py` |
| games DDL (ASR-1) | `sql/schema.sql`, `questions/repository.py` | `tests/test_persistence.py` |
| Component Game/Question/User/Admin | `game/`, `questions/`, `users/`, `admin/` packages | per-package tests |

# AGENT_NOTES — Space Fractions

Single-user Windows desktop app: educational fractions game for 6th graders (Space Fractions).

## Key decisions
- Tkinter UI, Python stdlib only, SQLite persistence (`data/spacefractions.db`), seed `data/questions.json` (20+ questions, 4 types).
- Components mirror UML packages: `game/` (Game, state machine, scoring), `questions/` (Question, checking with `fractions.Fraction`, repository), `users/`, `admin/`, `ui/`.
- Domain logic is pure Python (no Tkinter) — fully headless-testable. UI layer only calls into it.
- State machine: Playing ⇄ Paused → GameOver; invalid transitions raise `InvalidTransitionError`.
- Answer checking accepts equivalent fractions (2/4 == 1/2) via `fractions.Fraction`.
- Admin gated by PIN (default `space-admin`); builder `create_app(root)` builds UI without mainloop.

## Conventions
- Screen = one Frame class per file in `ui/`, switched by `ui/app.py` `App` controller.
- Factory `create_app(root)` exposed for smoke tests (never calls mainloop).
- Fonts: titles 36+, questions 30, inputs/buttons 20+. Theme: dark space blue `#0B1736`, accents yellow/cyan/pink/green.
- Window ≥1100x750, maximized on start, F11/Esc fullscreen.
- Tests: pytest, headless. UI smoke test uses ONE session-scoped Tk, retry 3x then skip on TclError, destroys children between tests.

## Data model
- `games` (id, game_state JSON), `questions` (id, prompt, type, options JSON, answer), `scores` (id, username, score, total, percentage, stars, timestamp).
